claim: SPY intraday momentum with a volatility-scaled opening-range breakout and trailing stop, 2007-2024, returns 19.6% annualized net of costs, Sharpe 1.33.
impact_on_spec: Primary literature basis for W4's single-ETF intraday momentum mechanism template: entry rule and volatility-scaled noise band.
limitations: Intraday opening-range strategy, not directly comparable to this project's daily-bar work; parameter ranges must be independently validated on SIP minute bars, not copied verbatim.

claim: Parameter optimization and alternative exit rules materially change intraday momentum strategy performance relative to the base Zarattini/Aziz/Barbon rule.
impact_on_spec: W4's parameter grid (noise-band multiplier x lookback x stop) must be treated as one mechanism family for effective-N clustering, not independent trials, given this paper's own finding that exit-rule choice alone materially moves results.
limitations: SSRN working paper, not yet peer-reviewed; treat magnitude claims as indicative, not as a validated benchmark to beat.

claim: A structural leakage-safe, search-aware evaluation harness rejected every LLM-discovered strategy across two frontier models, up to 100 candidates, 5 runs, on 453 stocks and 39 ETFs; passive benchmarks were certified with OOS confidence intervals excluding zero. Preregistered hypotheses face a lower evidential bar than brute search.
impact_on_spec: Justifies this week's overall strategy of re-validating an existing preregistered route (W3) and testing one literature-grounded mechanism (W4) rather than running a fresh search; directly supports the plan's ranking principle in section 1.
limitations: Findings are about LLM-discovered strategies specifically; this project's kernel search (GP/parameter mutation) is not LLM-driven, though the same search-vs-preregistration evidential-bar argument applies by extension.

claim: Centered temporal features and same-day-open execution using post-open daily-bar information cause large, stable inflation in both predictive and trading metrics; a clean t+1-open execution reference isolates this decision-time leakage from other evaluation-convention choices.
impact_on_spec: Independent external confirmation that this project's hard-coded signal_on=bar_close / fill_assumption=next_bar_open convention (StrategySpec.execution, Literal-only, no other value permitted) is a leakage-safety feature rather than an arbitrary constraint; no code change needed, cited as supporting evidence.
limitations: Benchmark paper studies a toggled synthetic setup, not this project's specific engine; the qualitative conclusion (same-day-open + post-open info is the dangerous pattern) is what transfers, not any specific magnitude.
